failure_case.summary: US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

result.why_top_candidate_wins: Chile Influenza Activity has the highest score (7) and the richest direct support in the subgraph: it is a leading indicator for the failed target (signal_us_hosp) and it is directly linked to the US mechanism (eq_us_flu_base) by both IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF edges. Those two mechanism-level links (+2 and +2) together with the leading-indicator relationship (+3) give it stronger and more mechanism-relevant pathways to explain an underpredicted, missed peak in US hospitalizations than the alternatives. Australia has only the leading-indicator and a possible-driver edge (total score 5) but lacks the explicit IMPORTATION_LINK into the US mechanism present for Chile. Travel Importation Pressure has importation/driver links (score 4) but lacks the explicit temporal leading-indicator connection to the US hospitalization signal that Chile provides. In short: Chile both precedes the target and is explicitly tied to the US mechanism, making it the most plausible single hidden driver given the graph evidence and ranking.
result.proposed_minimal_edit: Add an importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base: create or activate an edge eq_us_flu_base <--IMPORTATION_FORCING-- signal_chile_flu (with a single new scalar parameter representing importation-driven incidence multiplier or additive importation inflow to the transmission/process equations). Test model fit with this single parameter (and a short lag consistent with the LEADING_INDICATOR edge) to see if it explains the missed peak.
result.caveat: This recommendation is based solely on the provided subgraph and scores; the LEADING_INDICATOR and IMPORTATION_LINK edges imply correlation and a plausible pathway but do not prove causation. Empirical testing (parameter estimation, lag sensitivity, and out-of-sample validation) is required to confirm whether adding the Chile importation term actually resolves the underprediction.
